reason:
The stop is a race on the prime's shared records worktree, not an ended entry, and a plain re-launch of Land is safe.
Three runs on the prime commit to and push the shared branch main-weft in loomyard-weft.
This run's Land step created the status commit aa13796e at 11:09:17.639 (trace b8f7fbdbc337191a).
Run leftover-strands-and-runs (trace a22a28b5c65d9711) then committed 15c0ddfb on the same branch at 11:09:19.695 and pushed it at 11:09:22.995.
The pair push's pushRecordsSide (internal/fabricengine/pushanchored.go) got nil from the push, then ran HasUnpushed.
That check saw the other run's new commit 15c0ddfb not yet pushed, so it fell through to recordsSideNotLanded.
recordsSideNotLanded reports "ended on origin" as its fallback whenever no fresh deferred record is found.
The ended-entry check in checkOrigin/awaitOrigin applies only to a branch gone from origin.
main-weft is present on origin, at 15c0ddfb (git ls-remote), so the message is a fallback, not a real ended entry.
aa13796e is an ancestor of origin's main-weft, so this run's commit has landed and nothing of the run is stranded.
The local branch is now ahead by one commit, f5681c2d, which another run made; the next records push carries it.
Land failed at its opening status push, before pulling the prime, deploying or pruning, so re-running Land redoes no partial work.
The run is already at the Land row, so no goto is needed.
The misleading fallback message in fabricengine is outside this task's scope (shuttle prompt delivery), so I made no fix and no commit.
